mans search for meaning.title: Man's Search for Meaning
mans search for meaning.author: Viktor E. Frankl
mans search for meaning.why: A psychiatrist describes surviving Nazi camps and what kept people going; short, humane and widely recommended for finding meaning in suffering.

red rising.title: Red Rising
red rising.author: Pierce Brown
red rising.why: A miner on Mars infiltrates the ruling caste to overthrow it; fast and violent, popular with fans of The Hunger Games and epic fantasy.

my friends.title: My Friends
my friends.author: Fredrik Backman
my friends.why: Backman's novel about friendship and a painting that connects four teenagers; fans who read it praise its warmth and quotable lines.

hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.author: Douglas Adams
hitchhikers guide to the galaxy.why: An ordinary man is whisked off Earth moments before it is demolished; absurd, quotable comic science fiction readers love from childhood.

night circus.title: The Night Circus
night circus.author: Erin Morgenstern
night circus.why: Two young magicians are bound in a competition inside a mysterious travelling circus; dreamy and romantic, loved for its imagery.

moby dick.title: Moby-Dick
moby dick.author: Herman Melville
moby dick.why: Captain Ahab hunts the white whale; long and digressive but readers find it funny and sublime.

name of the wind.title: The Name of the Wind
name of the wind.author: Patrick Rothfuss
name of the wind.why: A gifted orphan grows into a legendary wizard, telling his own story; lyrical and absorbing, a fan favourite.

name of the rose.title: The Name of the Rose
name of the rose.author: Umberto Eco
name of the rose.why: A monk investigates murders in a medieval abbey; a learned detective story that readers find rewarding.

one hundred years of solitude.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
one hundred years of solitude.author: Gabriel García Márquez
one hundred years of solitude.why: Seven generations of a family in a Colombian village, full of magic and fate; the classic of magical realism.

shadow of the wind.title: The Shadow of the Wind
shadow of the wind.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
shadow of the wind.why: A boy finds a forgotten book in a Barcelona library of lost books and uncovers its author's mystery; gothic and bookish.

north woods.title: North Woods
north woods.author: Daniel Mason
north woods.why: Centuries of people who live in one New England house and the woods around it; beautifully written and varied.

crime and punishment.title: Crime and Punishment
crime and punishment.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
crime and punishment.why: A poor student commits murder and is consumed by guilt; psychological and intense, it leaves readers in a deep state.

god of small things.title: The God of Small Things
god of small things.author: Arundhati Roy
god of small things.why: Twins in Kerala grow up under the weight of a family tragedy; fascinating and poetic, though not an easy read.

pale fire.title: Pale Fire
pale fire.author: Vladimir Nabokov
pale fire.why: A poem and a madly unreliable commentary on it; a tricky, brilliant puzzle for readers who like playing with form.

glass castle.title: The Glass Castle
glass castle.author: Jeannette Walls
glass castle.why: The author grows up with brilliant but irresponsible parents who drag the family through poverty; compelling and easy to read.

swan song.title: Swan Song
swan song.author: Robert R. McCammon
swan song.why: Survivors of nuclear war fight over what remains of America and its soul; a huge post-apocalyptic story recommended after The Stand.

way of kings.title: The Way of Kings
way of kings.author: Brandon Sanderson
way of kings.why: Warriors, scholars and slaves are drawn into an ancient war on a storm-swept world; Sanderson's huge opening to a vast series.

perfume.title: Perfume
perfume.author: Patrick Süskind
perfume.why: A man with a perfect sense of smell turns to murder to create the ultimate scent; strange, vivid and haunting.

fifth season.title: The Fifth Season
fifth season.author: N. K. Jemisin
fifth season.why: People who can control the earth live in an apocalypse-prone world; inventive and gripping, a Hugo winner.

neuromancer.title: Neuromancer
neuromancer.author: William Gibson
neuromancer.why: A washed-up hacker is hired for one last job in cyberspace; the novel that invented cyberpunk, dense but influential.

doomsday book.title: Doomsday book
doomsday book.author: Connie Willis
doomsday book.why: A historian time-travels to medieval England just as the plague hits; readers say it will break your heart.

haunting of hill house.title: The Haunting of Hill House
haunting of hill house.author: Shirley Jackson
haunting of hill house.why: Four people spend a summer in a haunted mansion with a fragile guest; a masterclass in subtle, creeping dread.

metamorphosis.title: Metamorphosis
metamorphosis.author: Franz Kafka
metamorphosis.why: A man wakes up as a giant insect and his family turns away; very short, strange and widely read.

brave new world.title: Brave New World
brave new world.author: Aldous Huxley
brave new world.why: A future society engineered for happiness and control; a classic dystopia readers still find relevant.

im glad my mom died.title: I'm Glad My Mom Died
im glad my mom died.author: Jennette McCurdy
im glad my mom died.why: The former child actress writes frankly about her controlling mother and her own illness; readers find it raw and darkly funny.

gravitys rainbow.title: Gravity's Rainbow
gravitys rainbow.author: Thomas Pynchon
gravitys rainbow.why: A sprawling, bizarre novel set around V-2 rockets in World War II; famous as one of the hardest books to read.

dracula.title: Dracula
dracula.author: Bram Stoker
dracula.why: Told through letters and diaries, a band of friends hunts the vampire count; surprisingly a page turner.

siddhartha.title: Siddhartha
siddhartha.author: Hermann Hesse
siddhartha.why: A young man in ancient India searches for spiritual understanding; short and lyrical, loved by many and a little preachy to some.

library at mount char.title: The Library at Mount Char
library at mount char.author: Scott Hawkins
library at mount char.why: A group of people raised by a godlike figure are drawn into a struggle for his library; violent, strange and darkly funny.

to kill a mockingbird.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
to kill a mockingbird.author: Harper Lee
to kill a mockingbird.why: A girl in Alabama watches her lawyer father defend a Black man; a warm, moving classic about justice.

will of the many.title: The Will of the Many
will of the many.author: James Islington
will of the many.why: An orphan enters an elite Roman-style academy where the powerful drain others' will; readers call it a gripping start to a series.

shes come undone.title: She's Come Undone
shes come undone.author: Wally Lamb
shes come undone.why: A troubled young woman recounts her difficult life with humour and pain; a popular emotional read.

terror.title: The Terror
terror.author: Dan Simmons
terror.why: Two ships are trapped in Arctic ice in 1845 and something hunts the crew; fiction based on a true expedition that readers cannot put down.

wuthering heights.title: Wuthering Heights
wuthering heights.author: Emily Brontë
wuthering heights.why: An obsessive love between Heathcliff and Cathy destroys two families on the Yorkshire moors; stormy and passionate.

braiding sweetgrass.title: Braiding Sweetgrass
braiding sweetgrass.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
braiding sweetgrass.why: A botanist and Potawatomi writer joins plant science with indigenous wisdom; readers love it, especially as an audiobook.

hobbit.title: The Hobbit
hobbit.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
hobbit.why: A comfort-loving hobbit is swept into a quest with dwarves to win back treasure from a dragon; a warm, easy adventure.

replay.title: Replay
replay.author: Ken Grimwood
replay.why: A man dies at 43 and wakes up as his 18-year-old self, again and again; an emotional time-loop story.

devil in the white city.title: The Devil in the White City
devil in the white city.author: Erik Larson
devil in the white city.why: The 1893 Chicago World's Fair is told alongside a serial killer working nearby; narrative history that reads like a thriller.

great alone.title: The Great Alone
great alone.author: Kristin Hannah
great alone.why: A family seeks a new start in the Alaskan wilderness, but the father unravels; readers find it gripping and emotional.

handmaids tale.title: The Handmaid's Tale
handmaids tale.author: Margaret Atwood
handmaids tale.why: In a theocratic America women are reduced to childbearing; chilling, widely recommended dystopia.

magus.title: The Magus
magus.author: John Fowles
magus.why: A young teacher on a Greek island is drawn into an elaborate psychological game; readers call it a crazy, gripping mystery.

hike.title: The Hike
hike.author: Drew Magary
hike.why: A man on a walk in the woods enters a surreal world of monsters and puzzles; quick and wildly inventive.

idiot.title: The Idiot
idiot.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
idiot.why: A kind prince returns to Russian society and everything around him turns tragic; some readers find it funny; long and demanding.

atmosphere.title: Atmosphere
atmosphere.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
atmosphere.why: A love story set among women astronauts in the early shuttle era; popular and easy to read.

buffalo hunter hunter.title: The Buffalo Hunter Hunter
buffalo hunter hunter.author: Stephen Graham Jones
buffalo hunter hunter.why: A priest's journals from the 1910s describe a vampire in Montana and the Blackfeet nation; an excellent, unsettling horror novel.

atonement.title: Atonement
atonement.author: Ian McEwan
atonement.why: A child's false accusation wrecks lives, and she spends her life atoning; admired for its ending, though a few readers find it slow.

oryx and crake.title: Oryx and Crake
oryx and crake.author: Margaret Atwood
oryx and crake.why: A lone survivor recalls the genetic engineering world that ended humanity; sharp dystopia that starts the MaddAddam trilogy.

remarkably bright creatures.title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
remarkably bright creatures.author: Shelby Van Pelt
remarkably bright creatures.why: A widow befriends a clever aquarium octopus who knows a secret; a heartwarming, easy read.

cats cradle.title: Cat's Cradle
cats cradle.author: Kurt Vonnegut
cats cradle.why: A writer searches for the inventor of the atom bomb and finds a made-up religion; short, dark and funny.

ishmael.title: Ishmael
ishmael.author: Daniel Quinn
ishmael.why: The comments mostly mix it up with another book of the same name, so there is no clear recommendation.

bluest eye.title: The Bluest Eye
bluest eye.author: Toni Morrison
bluest eye.why: A Black girl in 1940s Ohio longs for blue eyes; short and painful, often recommended for its beautiful prose.

say nothing.title: Say Nothing
say nothing.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
say nothing.why: The story of a woman taken during the Northern Ireland Troubles and the people behind her murder; gripping and surprising narrative history.

recursion.title: Recursion
recursion.author: Blake Crouch
recursion.why: A memory-altering disease and a time device unravel reality; a fast thriller that suckers readers in.

verity.title: Verity
verity.author: Colleen Hoover
verity.why: A writer finishing another author's series finds a disturbing manuscript; an addictive, trashy thriller that kept readers up.

mistborn.title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
mistborn.author: Brandon Sanderson
mistborn.why: A street thief joins a crew to overthrow an immortal ruler using metal-based magic; inventive and fast, with a great twist.

picture of dorian gray.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
picture of dorian gray.author: Oscar Wilde
picture of dorian gray.why: The comments are mostly negative, with readers annoyed or giving up early.

tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.author: Gabrielle Zevin
tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.why: Two friends build video games across decades; warm and moving story about creativity and friendship.

anxious people.title: Anxious People
anxious people.author: Fredrik Backman
anxious people.why: A failed bank robbery turns into a hostage situation at an apartment viewing; comic and warm.

covenant of water.title: The Covenant of Water
covenant of water.author: Abraham Verghese
covenant of water.why: Three generations of a Kerala family linked by a curse and by medicine; long, rich and beautifully written.

all systems red.title: All Systems Red
all systems red.author: Martha Wells
all systems red.why: A security robot hacks its own controls and just wants to watch shows; short, charming and quick to read.

song of achilles.title: The Song of Achilles
song of achilles.author: Madeline Miller
song of achilles.why: The love story of Achilles and Patroclus at Troy, told by Patroclus; readers find it beautiful and heartbreaking.

misery.title: Misery
misery.author: Stephen King
misery.why: A writer is held captive by his number one fan; a tight, scary thriller recommended to anyone starting with King.

shining.title: The Shining
shining.author: Stephen King
shining.why: A struggling writer takes a winter caretaker job at an isolated hotel; the novel is scarier than the film.

martyr.title: Martyr!
martyr.author: Kaveh Akbar
martyr.why: A recovering addict and poet searches for meaning in death; readers rate it highly as a recent standout.

snow crash.title: Snow Crash
snow crash.author: Neal Stephenson
snow crash.why: A pizza-delivering hacker fights a virus in the metaverse; funny, fast-moving cyberpunk.

giver.title: The Giver
giver.author: Lois Lowry
giver.why: A boy discovers the secret behind his perfectly controlled community; a short school favourite that adults say they would re-read.

wild.title: Wild
wild.author: Cheryl Strayed
wild.why: After her mother's death and her marriage collapse, the author hikes the Pacific Crest Trail; moving and beautifully written.

giovannis room.title: Giovanni's Room
giovannis room.author: James Baldwin
giovannis room.why: An American in Paris struggles with desire and shame; short and intense, readers say it blew them away.

lathe of heaven.title: The Lathe of Heaven
lathe of heaven.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
lathe of heaven.why: A man whose dreams change reality has a therapist who wants to use them; a short, odd, thoughtful book.

perdido street station.title: Perdido Street Station
perdido street station.author: China Miéville
perdido street station.why: A scientist unleashes a monster in the strange city of New Crobuzon; dense, inventive new weird fantasy.
